geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the dominant solid with a courtyard/public-void macro so the access edge can read as an active threshold.
Enlarge the public void enough to register in all views as a meaningful court rather than a shallow notch.
Align the opening with the program-frame access side to restore frontage logic.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the current courtyard logic with a stronger, access-aligned public void to produce a legible ground threshold.
Increase the void size enough to read as usable public space rather than a minor subtraction.
Open the court toward the verified access side in the program frame so the frontage becomes semantically public.
Lower the terrace link to strengthen ground contact and make the entry seam more legible at street level.

rationale: The candidate is coherent across views as one dominant bent/bar-like mass with a stepped end and a small carved/terraced response, so it avoids the fragmented or colliding-solids failure. The plan and elevations show a readable dominant gesture, but the open-space figure is weak: the blue frontage edge is not strongly answered by a clear public void, entry seam, or undercut, so the access relationship feels only loosely engaged. Parcel containment appears respected and the form is not merely a box, but the mass still reads more like a compact sculpted object than a fully activated neighborhood-living threshold. Programmatically, it can plausibly support mixed neighborhood living/commercial use because the section is continuous and the top mass is calm, though the frontage/public-space logic should be strengthened. For next iteration, preserve the dominant bent bar, but carve a more legible court/notch or terrace aligned to the access edge and avoid over-fractionating the body.
